title: Peritonitis: Guarding, Rigidity and Rebound Tenderness
subject: Surgical Triads
preview: Peritonitis may cause involuntary guarding, rigidity, rebound tenderness and pain on movement.
quickRevision: Peritonitis may cause involuntary guarding, rigidity, rebound tenderness and pain on movement.
Analgesia and resuscitation should not be withheld while obtaining clinical and surgical assessment.
Peritoneal signs may be subtle in older adults, immunosuppressed patients or those receiving steroids.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Peritonitis may cause involuntary guarding, rigidity, rebound tenderness and pain on movement.
A rigid abdomen in an unstable patient raises concern for serious intra-abdominal pathology such as perforation.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Analgesia and resuscitation should not be withheld while obtaining clinical and surgical assessment.
Peritoneal signs may be subtle in older adults, immunosuppressed patients or those receiving steroids.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Rebound tenderness alone cannot establish the exact cause or site of abdominal pathology.
